football_evidence.question: Can TCU take away West Virginia’s big plays?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward TCU, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.9 of the 4.3 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When TCU has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): TCU’s offense averages 8.5 yards per pass attempt, and West Virginia’s defense allows 11.2 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When TCU has the ball (big plays through the air): TCU’s offense turns 12.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and West Virginia’s defense gives up explosive gains on 19.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When West Virginia has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): West Virginia’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.5% of its dropbacks, and TCU’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When West Virginia has the ball (big plays on the ground): West Virginia’s offense turns 7.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and TCU’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
contradicting: When TCU has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): TCU’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.1% of its dropbacks, and West Virginia’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When West Virginia has the ball (big plays through the air): West Virginia’s offense turns 22.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and TCU’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When TCU has the ball (big plays on the ground): TCU’s offense turns 2.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and West Virginia’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When TCU has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): TCU’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 22.2% of its runs, and West Virginia’s defense stops 19.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
quarterbacks: Jaden Craig has completed 128 of 192 passes (66.7%) for 1,687 yards, 8.8 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for TCU, and has been sacked on 17 of 209 dropbacks.

Michael Hawkins Jr. has completed 83 of 144 passes (57.6%) for 1,519 yards, 10.5 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 1 interception in seven games for West Virginia, and has been sacked on 12 of 156 dropbacks.
